stewart_read: Customer discloses an existing energy arrangement tied to Xcel that could materially affect design/net-metering, and the rep just logs it without asking what company runs it or how it works.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep could be deliberately deferring detail to the closer/specialist since this is technical territory outside setter scope.
coaching_implication: A quick clarifying question ('is that a subscription program, and do you know the company?') would give the closer far more to work with and shows engagement rather than filing the detail silently.

stewart_read: A warm referral from a family member already in the pipeline is a strong qualifying signal — this customer is pre-sold on legitimacy.
coaching_implication: Rep should have leaned into this warmth by asking what the father-in-law told him about the process, deepening rapport instead of pivoting immediately to referral-bonus logistics.

quote: So, yeah, we do have referral bonuses. So,
stewart_read: Rep spends the opening moments on referral-bonus administration rather than exploring the customer's actual interest or bill pain, a low-value use of the first minute.
alternative_hypothesis: This could be a legitimate quick housekeeping step before returning to qualification, which the rep does do next.
coaching_implication: Keep referral-bonus mechanics brief; get to the interest/bill anchor faster to use the customer's warmth while it's highest.

quote: Great. So you can either text or email it over to me, whichever one works better for you.
stewart_read: The rep never got an actual bill number or kWh figure on the call — the bill was deferred entirely to a future email, so there is no anchor to flip.
alternative_hypothesis: Given the customer stated he was at work and couldn't pull up the bill, deferring to email was a reasonable practical accommodation rather than a rep failure.
coaching_implication: Even without the document, rep could have asked 'roughly what do you pay a month?' to get a verbal anchor before falling back to the email path.

quote: a two or 3PM work good for you and your wife?
stewart_read: Rep correctly folds the wife into the appointment-setting question rather than booking around her, matching the schema's positive pattern.
coaching_implication: Good execution — reinforce this as the standard move for any identified co-owner.

quote: Alright. Sounds great. Thanks for your help.
stewart_read: Call closes without the rep explicitly asking 'is that fair?' or reconfirming the no-driving/computer requirement, leaving the button-up incomplete per verified events (button_up partial).
alternative_hypothesis: The overall warmth and customer's own enthusiastic close ('sounds great') may have made the formal handshake feel unnecessary in the moment.
coaching_implication: Always land the explicit verbal handshake and computer/no-driving instruction regardless of how warm the customer sounds — it's the show-rate lever, not a formality.
